groups.title: Nuts
groups.explanation: Each of these is sold as a nut, whatever a botanist might call it.

groups.title: Shades of brown
groups.explanation: All four are browns, from a painter's umber to the soft grey of taupe.

groups.title: Broadleaf trees
groups.explanation: These broadleaf trees have grown in British woods for thousands of years.

sources.excerpt: All commercially grown almonds sold as food in the U.S.
In 2023, 3.9 million tons of cashew nuts were harvested globally, led by the Ivory Coast and India.
The pecan is the state nut of Alabama, Arkansas, California, Texas, and Louisiana, and is also the state tree of Texas.
Nuts of the eastern black walnut (Juglans nigra) and butternuts (Juglans cinerea) are less commonly consumed.
This version of the color raw umber has a hue of 33, and is classified as an orange-brown.
Sepia is a reddish-brown color, named after the rich brown pigment derived from the ink sac of the common cuttlefish Sepia.
The color taupe is a representation of the average color of the fur of the French mole.
Fawn is a light yellowish tan colour.
Individual oak trees of cultural significance include the Royal Oak in Britain, the Charter Oak in the United States, and the Guernica Oak in the Basque Country.
An oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
Elms are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.
Willows, also called sallows and osiers, of the genus Salix, comprise around 350 species (plus numerous hybrids) of typically deciduous trees and shrubs.
